# CSP formalization:
# Variables:
#   start: minute-of-day when the meeting starts on Monday
#   end: start + meeting duration
#
# Constraints:
#   - Work hours are 09:00 to 17:00.
#   - Meeting duration is 30 minutes.
#   - Deborah has no blocked intervals.
#   - Albert is blocked during:
#       09:00 to 10:00
#       10:30 to 12:00
#       15:00 to 16:30
#   - Albert cannot meet after 11:00, so the meeting must end by 11:00.
#
# Search:
#   Try start times from 09:00 in one-minute increments and select
#   the earliest start time satisfying all constraints.

def to_minutes(hh, mm=0):
    return hh * 60 + mm

DAY = "Monday"
DURATION = 30
WORK_START = to_minutes(9)
WORK_END = to_minutes(17)

busy_intervals = {
    "Deborah": [],
    "Albert": [
        (to_minutes(9), to_minutes(10)),
        (to_minutes(10, 30), to_minutes(12)),
        (to_minutes(15), to_minutes(16, 30)),
    ],
}

latest_end = {
    "Deborah": WORK_END,
    "Albert": to_minutes(11),
}

def feasible(start):
    end = start + DURATION

    if end > WORK_END:
        return False

    for person in busy_intervals:
        if end > latest_end[person]:
            return False

        for block_start, block_end in busy_intervals[person]:
            if start < block_end and end > block_start:
                return False

    return True

for start in range(WORK_START, WORK_END - DURATION + 1):
    if feasible(start):
        end = start + DURATION
        start_str = f"{start // 60:02d}:{start % 60:02d}"
        end_str = f"{end // 60:02d}:{end % 60:02d}"
        print([DAY, start_str, end_str])

# Variables: start, end (minutes from midnight)
# Constraints:
# - Monday work hours: 09:00 <= start < end <= 17:00
# - duration = 30 minutes
# - no overlap with participant busy intervals
# - preference: no new meeting time after 12:30 (end <= 12:30)

def to_minutes(value):
    hour, minute = value.split(':')
    return int(hour) * 60 + int(minute)

def format_time(minutes):
    return f"{minutes // 60:02d}:{minutes % 60:02d}"

day = "Monday"
work_start = to_minutes("09:00")
work_end = to_minutes("17:00")
duration = 30
preference_limit = to_minutes("12:30")

schedules = {
    "Jack": [
        ("09:30", "10:30"),
        ("11:00", "11:30"),
        ("12:30", "13:00"),
        ("14:00", "14:30"),
        ("16:00", "16:30"),
    ],
    "Charlotte": [
        ("09:30", "10:00"),
        ("10:30", "12:00"),
        ("12:30", "13:30"),
        ("14:00", "16:00"),
    ],
}

busy_intervals = {
    name: [(to_minutes(s), to_minutes(e)) for s, e in intervals]
    for name, intervals in schedules.items()
}

def conflicts(start, end, intervals):
    for s, e in intervals:
        if start < e and s < end:
            return True
    return False

best = None
for start in range(work_start, work_end - duration + 1):
    end = start + duration
    if end > work_end:
        break
    if end > preference_limit:
        continue
    feasible = True
    for name in busy_intervals:
        if conflicts(start, end, busy_intervals[name]):
            feasible = False
            break
    if feasible:
        best = (start, end)
        break

if best is None:
    # Fallback: if the preference is treated as soft, choose earliest hard-feasible time.
    for start in range(work_start, work_end - duration + 1):
        end = start + duration
        feasible = True
        for name in busy_intervals:
            if conflicts(start, end, busy_intervals[name]):
                feasible = False
                break
        if feasible:
            best = (start, end)
            break

start, end = best
print([day, format_time(start), format_time(end)])
```

work_end = to_min("17:00")

        ("Tuesday", [("10:30", "11:00"), ("15:00", "15:30")]),
        ("Wednesday", [("10:00", "11:00"), ("11:30", "12:00"), ("12:30", "13:00"), ("13:30", "14:00"), ("15:00", "15:30"), ("16:00", "16:30")]),
    ],
    "Ralph": [
        ("Monday", [("10:00", "13:30"), ("14:00", "14:30"), ("15:00", "17:00")]),
        ("Tuesday", [("9:00", "9:30"), ("10:00", "10:30"), ("11:00", "11:30"), ("12:00", "13:00"), ("14:00", "15:30"), ("16:00", "17:00")]),

busy = {day: [] for day in days}
for person, entries in raw_schedules.items():

    for bs, be in busy[day]:
        if start < be and end > bs:
            return True
    return False

    end = start + duration
    if end > work_end:

    return not conflicts(day, start, end)

            best = (day, start, start + duration)
            break
    if best:
        break

if best:
    print([best[0], to_str(best[1]), to_str(best[2])])
else:
    print([])

import sys

DURATION = 30

PREFERENCE_NOT_AFTER = 13 * 60

...

def hhmm(minutes):
    return f"{minutes // 60:02d}:{minutes % 60:02d}"

def free_at(person, start, end):
    for b_start, b_end in busy.get(person, []):
        if start < b_end and end > b_start:
            return False
    return True

def meets_all(start, end, require_preference):
    if start < WORK_START or end > WORK_END:
        return False
    if require_preference and end > PREFERENCE_NOT_AFTER:
        return False
    return all(free_at(person, start, end) for person in busy)

def search(require_preference):
    for start in range(WORK_START, WORK_END - DURATION + 1):
        end = start + DURATION
        if meets_all(start, end, require_preference):
            return start, end
    return None

result = search(True)
if result is None:
    result = search(False)
if result is not None:
    start, end = result
    print([DAY, hhmm(start), hhmm(end)])

DURATION = 30

UNAVAILABLE = {

        "Monday": [

            (12 * 60, 12 * 60 + 30),

            (16 * 60 + 30, 17 * 60),

def overlaps(a_start, a_end, b_start, b_end):

    if start < WORK_START or end > WORK_END:

def preference_penalty(day, start, end):

# Formalization:
# Variable:
#   start: start time of the meeting in minutes from midnight on Monday
#
# Domain:
#   work_start <= start <= work_end - duration
#
# Constraints:
#   1. The meeting is exactly `duration` minutes long.
#   2. The meeting must lie completely within work hours.
#   3. For every participant, the meeting interval must not overlap any busy interval.
#   4. Helen cannot meet after 15:00, so the meeting must end no later than 15:00.


def fmt(minutes):
    """Convert minutes from midnight to zero-padded HH:MM."""
    return f"{minutes // 60:02d}:{minutes % 60:02d}"


def overlaps(start_a, end_a, start_b, end_b):
    """Return True if half-open intervals [start_a, end_a) and [start_b, end_b) overlap."""
    return start_a < end_b and start_b < end_a


def solve():
    day = "Monday"
    duration = 30

    work_start = 9 * 60
    work_end = 17 * 60

    participants = ["Christine", "Helen"]

    busy_intervals = {
        "Christine": [
            (11 * 60, 11 * 60 + 30),
            (15 * 60, 15 * 60 + 30),
        ],
        "Helen": [
            (9 * 60 + 30, 10 * 60 + 30),
            (11 * 60, 11 * 60 + 30),
            (12 * 60, 12 * 60 + 30),
            (13 * 60 + 30, 16 * 60),
            (16 * 60 + 30, 17 * 60),
        ],
    }

    # Additional preferences/constraints specific to named participants.
    preferences = {
        "Helen": {
            "latest_end": 15 * 60,
        }
    }

    # Search all possible one-minute-aligned start times.
    for start in range(work_start, work_end - duration + 1):
        end = start + duration
        valid = True

        for person in participants:
            # Check participant-specific preferences.
            pref = preferences.get(person, {})
            if "latest_end" in pref and end > pref["latest_end"]:
                valid = False
                break

            # Check existing busy intervals for this participant.
            for busy_start, busy_end in busy_intervals.get(person, []):
                if overlaps(start, end, busy_start, busy_end):
                    valid = False
                    break

            if not valid:
                break

        if valid:
            return [day, fmt(start), fmt(end)]

    return None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    answer = solve()
    if answer is None:
        raise SystemExit(1)
    print(answer)

                    break
            if not feasible:

            start_str = f"{start // 60:02d}:{start % 60:02d}"
            end_str = f"{end // 60:02d}:{end % 60:02d}"
            print([day_str, start_str, end_str])
            break
    else:
        continue
    break

import sys

def to_minutes(hhmm):

days = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday"]
work_start = 9*60
work_end = 17*60
duration = 30

                (to_minutes("13:00"), to_minutes("13:30")),
                (to_minutes("14:30"), to_minutes("15:00"))],
    "Wednesday": []
  },
  "Joyce": {
    "Monday": [(to_minutes("9:00"), to_minutes("9:30")),
               (to_minutes("10:00"), to_minutes("11:00")),
               (to_minutes("11:30"), to_minutes("12:30")),
               (to_minutes("13:00"), to_minutes("15:00")),
               (to_minutes("15:30"), to_minutes("17:00"))],
    "Tuesday": [(to_minutes("9:00"), to_minutes("17:00"))],
    "Wednesday": [(to_minutes("9:00"), to_minutes("9:30")),
                  (to_minutes("10:00"), to_minutes("11:00")),

def preference_violated(day, start):
    if day == "Monday" and start < 12*60:
        return True
    return False

def is_free(person, day, start, end):
    for bs, be in busy[person].get(day, []):
        if start < be and bs < end:
            return False
    return True

def candidate_valid(day, start, end, enforce_preference):
    if not (work_start <= start and end <= work_end): return False
    if day not in days: return False
    if required_day is not None and day != required_day: return False
    for person in busy:
        if not is_free(person, day, start, end): return False
    if enforce_preference and preference_violated(day, start): return False
    return True

def solve():
    candidates = []
    for day in days:
        if required_day is not None and day != required_day:
            continue
        for start in range(work_start, work_end - duration + 1):
            end = start + duration
            if candidate_valid(day, start, end, True):
                return [day, fmt(start), fmt(end)]
    # fallback if preference would eliminate all solutions
    for day in days:

            end = start + duration
            if candidate_valid(day, start, end, False):
                return [day, fmt(start), fmt(end)]
    return None

if __name__ == "__main__":
    result = solve()
    # The problem statement guarantees a solution exists.
